stem: Which Grignard reagent gives 2,2-dimethylpropanoic acid after treatment with $\text{CO}_2$ followed by acidic hydrolysis?

verdicts.working: CO₂ adds one carboxyl carbon to the Grignard group: (CH₃)₃C–MgBr → (CH₃)₃C–COOH.

working:
$\text{R–MgBr} + \text{CO}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{O}^+} \text{R–COOH}$
For 2,2-dimethylpropanoic acid, $\text{R}=(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}$. The required reagent is $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C–MgBr}$.

Independent check: CO₂ adds one carboxyl carbon to the Grignard group: (CH₃)₃C–MgBr → (CH₃)₃C–COOH.
solution:
Grignard carboxylation gives $\text{R–MgBr} \xrightarrow{\text{CO}_2,\,\text{H}_3\text{O}^+} \text{R–COOH}$, adding one carbon as the carboxyl group.
For 2,2-dimethylpropanoic acid, $\text{R}=(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}$; hence the reagent is $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C–MgBr}$, tert-butylmagnesium bromide.
